title: RAW UNREVIEWED: f69r wind labels name source or destination bearings
summary: The admitted f69r outer text ring has sixteen owned sectors and a separate twelve-part colored wind skeleton. A wind reading could name where air comes from or where it travels; the two conventions reverse a direction even when the same compass spoke is drawn. Before assigning any Voynich label, find a complete dated wind primary with explicit source/destination language and a fixed orientation marker, then freeze its cardinal and collateral bearings and all f69r sector owners. Test the complete ring under both polarities with one constant rotation and handedness. If the manuscript has no independent orientation anchor or if both polarities fit equally, record no semantic discrimination. This does not rerun the closed four-versus-twelve phase or cross-ring label-profile tests.

design.mechanism: source-bearing and destination-bearing semantics give opposite directions for one owned wind label
design.unit: complete admitted f69r sixteen-sector outer ring plus the separately owned twelve-part interior
design.contrast: wind origin bearing versus travel destination bearing under fixed compass orientation
design.prediction: one predeclared whole-ring reading and independently fixed orientation resolve the polarity consistently at all eligible sectors; missing orientation or equal fits mean no capacity
